sources.name: CES 2022 weighted historical demographic vote estimates (cumulative v10)
sources.notes: Shiro Kuriwaki, Cumulative CES Common Content, DOI10.7910/DVN/II2DB6 v10; Berkeley SDA mirror. Self-reported Democratic/(Democratic+Republican) vote, age25+, race_h any-part Hispanic-exclusive categories, standardized sex. Two education levels: high school or less, some college or more. Middle Eastern respondents join White to align legacy ACS race definitions. Weight=weight_post. Raw or Kish effective n<30 suppressed. National Senate/governor averages cover states holding that office. District estimates are descriptive and are not district-representative samples. Kish effective n does not account for full survey design.

sources.name: CES 2024 weighted historical demographic vote estimates (cumulative v10)
sources.notes: Shiro Kuriwaki, Cumulative CES Common Content, DOI10.7910/DVN/II2DB6 v10; Berkeley SDA mirror. Self-reported Democratic/(Democratic+Republican) vote, age25+, race_h any-part Hispanic-exclusive categories, standardized sex. Two education levels: high school or less, some college or more. Middle Eastern respondents join White to align legacy ACS race definitions. Weight=weight. Raw or Kish effective n<30 suppressed. National Senate/governor averages cover states holding that office. District estimates are descriptive and are not district-representative samples. Kish effective n does not account for full survey design. 2024 v10 predates vote validation and lacks post-wave weights; normal pre-wave weight used per guide, with residual attrition risk.

limitations: Scope: 435 voting House seats, regularly scheduled Senate elections and verified Senate specials, and state governors. Candidates, delegates, territories, and state/local offices are not yet loaded.
ACS education intersections describe residents age 25+, including noncitizens. They are not counts of eligible or likely voters, and exclude voters age 18–24.
Census sex is not a measure of gender identity. Race categories include people of Hispanic ethnicity; Hispanic origin is a separate concept.

House projections use 119th-Congress population and geographic baselines as proxies where 2026 boundaries changed. The House map is a seat cartogram and does not present older boundaries as current ones.
Ballots do not record race, sex, or education. Historical demographic vote shares are weighted survey estimates, not official demographic returns. Small samples are suppressed.
The 2024 demographic baseline is fitted to CES responses. News response coefficients are explicit priors; no historically calibrated causal news effect or election win probability is claimed.
Forecasts combine mutually exclusive Hispanic/non-Hispanic cohorts. Nonwhite Hispanic allocation is estimated within each sex and education cell; uncertainty in this bridge is not measured.
Predicted race shares are population-standardized preferences for adults age 25+ under equal-turnout assumptions, an experimental proxy for the full electorate.
Two-party vote share excludes other candidates. State-level history cannot be substituted for congressional-district observations without a labeled model.

news_response.group_signal: group coverage direction minus overall party direction (deviation from the national environment)
news_response.national_distribution: CES 2016->2018 cell response ratios (data/model/demographic_elasticity.json), normalized so the national population-weighted shift equals the national swing

uncertainty.basis: Race SD: robust spread of Senate-minus-presidential margins, MEDSL 2010-2024 (House shares the Senate value; governor widened by assumption). National SD: assumed error of the news-implied national environment.

anchoring.method: Per race, one logit offset added to every cohort so the population-weighted 2024 baseline equals the actual 2024 presidential two-party result (2026 district lines where redrawn).

validation.method: Deterministic 80/20 respondent holdout; all office votes from a respondent stay together.
validation.scope: Same-election 2024 survey response validation only; not 2026 race accuracy or historical news validation.
